data.body:
MEASURED BEDROCK FINDINGS — real AWS calls, account 5797...98, profile frontier, region us-east-2, via boto3 Converse and pydantic-ai BedrockConverseModel. Oracle: same request twice with a cachePoint after a ~4000-token stable system prefix; read cacheReadInputTokens/cacheWriteInputTokens off the real response (no latency inference).

1) ON-DEMAND MODEL IDS ARE NOT INVOKABLE HERE AT ALL. Both anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6 and the old anthropic.claude-3-haiku-20240307-v1:0 return ValidationException: 'Invocation of model ID ... with on-demand throughput isnt supported. Retry your request with the ID or ARN of an inference profile.' So this storys framing — compare a plain on-demand id against an inference-profile ARN and pick — is moot in this environment: only inference profiles work. rebars documented default MUST be an inference-profile id.

2) PROMPT CACHING WORKS WITH A REGIONAL INFERENCE PROFILE. us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6: attempt 1 cache_write=4017 cache_read=0; attempt 2 cache_write=0 cache_read=4017. Reproducible — a later run hit a still-warm cache (cache_read=4017 on attempt 1, 5-min TTL). This REFUTES the premise of pydantic-ai #4381 (that a cross-region inference profile silently breaks caching) for this model/region.

3) CACHING IS MODEL-DEPENDENT AND FAILS SILENTLY. us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-5-20251101-v1:0 AND global.anthropic.claude-opus-4-5-20251101-v1:0 both returned cache_read=0 AND cache_write=0 on both attempts, with the full 4029 input tokens billed every call — no error, no warning. CORRECTION TO MY OWN FIRST INFERENCE: I initially attributed this to the global. prefix; a controlled same-model comparison (us. vs global. for opus-4-5) showed BOTH fail, so the discriminator is the MODEL, not the profile prefix. This silent double-billing is the real hazard #4381 is circling.

4) Haiku 3 + cachePoint hard-fails: us.anthropic.claude-3-haiku-20240307-v1:0 -> AccessDeniedException You invoked an unsupported model or your request did not allow prompt caching.

5) NEW, HIGH SEVERITY, NOT IN THIS PLAN — TEMPERATURE IS FATAL ON BEDROCK FOR SOME MODELS. us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7 with temperature=0 -> ValidationException/400 temperature is deprecated for this model; the identical call WITHOUT temperature succeeds. Confirmed through pydantic-ai too: BedrockConverseModel + BedrockModelSettings(temperature=0.0) -> ModelHTTPError status_code 400; without temperature -> OK.

Why this breaks rebar on Bedrock: runner.py sets model_settings[temperature] whenever cfg.temperature or req.config.temperature is set, and the plan-review Pass-2 verify steps deliberately send temperature=0 (greedy, so re-verifying a finding does not resample). pydantic-ais _drop_unsupported_sampling_settings exists ONLY in models/anthropic.py — NOT in models/bedrock.py (grepped) — so the direct-Anthropic path is protected (it warns Sampling parameters [temperature] are not supported ... will be ignored) and the Bedrock path is NOT. A Bedrock gate run on such a model therefore hard-fails rather than degrading.

CONSEQUENCES THIS PLAN MUST ABSORB BEFORE IMPLEMENTATION:
- default/documented model id must be an inference profile, and us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6 is the VERIFIED caching default;
- caching must be measured per model, and because failure is silent, rebar should WARN when caching was requested but cache_read and cache_write are both 0 (an analogue of the existing _warn_if_zeroed_usage), otherwise operators silently pay full input on every call;
- the Bedrock builder must not send an unsupported sampling parameter. This needs a real decision (omit temperature on Bedrock, gate it on a capability, or pin supported models) — it cannot be left to the implementer, and it directly threatens story eb6e (S8, production review-bot cutover with no Anthropic fallback).

Raw probe scripts: /Users/joeoakhart/.claude/jobs/4ca991d2/tmp/bedrock_cache_probe.py (+probe2/3/4 variants).
